standard_prerequisites.name: Left and right conditional rules
standard_prerequisites.statement: Left-if derives (A implies B) on the left from B on the left and A on the right; Right-if derives (A implies B) on the right from A on the left and B on the right.
standard_prerequisites.use: Item (1) uses Left-if on the initial sequents; item (2) chains Left-not, Left-exchange, Right-weakening and Right-if in the first tree, and Left-weakening plus Right-if in the second.

core_obligations: Statement (prop at 1079, three labels on one statement/proof span): (1) A, A implies B proves B; (2) both (not A) proves A implies B and B proves A implies B.
Item (1) (proof from 1086): one derivation applying Left-if to the initial sequents A sequent A and B sequent B, yielding A implies B, A sequent B.

Item (2) (proof from 1092): two derivations. First: Left-not on A sequent A, Left-exchange, Right-weakening to add B on the right, then Right-if, yielding (not A) sequent A implies B. Second: Left-weakening to add A on the left of B sequent B, then Right-if, yielding B sequent A implies B.
proof_roadmap: Witness item (1) with the Left-if binary derivation.
Witness the not-A half of item (2) with the four-inference chain ending in Right-if.
Witness the B half of item (2) with Left-weakening plus Right-if.
difficulty_reason: Conditional provability facts (statement 1079-1084, proof 1086-1112): all three derivations carried in span; substantive step is the four-inference chain (Left-not, Left-exchange, Right-weakening, Right-if) in item (2). H2.
